problem_text:
A logistics company needs to schedule 6 delivery routes through 6 different distribution centers.

Each route consists of a sequence of stops represented as pairs (Center, Handling time),
where each pair specifies the distribution center where the stop must occur and the amount of time required for handling.
The order of pairs indicates the required sequence in which the stops must be completed.

Route details:
* R1 requires the sequence: (C6, 7) → (C1, 5) → (C3, 7) → (C4, 4) → (C2, 6) → (C5, 3)
* R2 requires the sequence: (C2, 10) → (C1, 7) → (C3, 8) → (C5, 2) → (C4, 2) → (C6, 7)
* R3 requires the sequence: (C5, 3) → (C6, 4) → (C2, 1) → (C1, 9) → (C3, 3) → (C4, 8)
* R4 requires the sequence: (C3, 7) → (C5, 5) → (C6, 3) → (C4, 6) → (C2, 9) → (C1, 6)
* R5 requires the sequence: (C5, 7) → (C2, 6) → (C4, 7) → (C3, 8) → (C6, 9) → (C1, 5)
* R6 requires the sequence: (C4, 1) → (C6, 10) → (C1, 10) → (C3, 9) → (C5, 2) → (C2, 4)

Each handling operation must run continuously once it begins and cannot be interrupted,
and each distribution center can only handle one delivery vehicle at a time.
The objective is to determine the processing order of all handling operations at the centers
so that the total completion time for all delivery routes is minimized.
